title: 1 Samuel Chapter 27 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 27 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 27 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 27.

questions.question: Why did David decide to escape to the land of the Philistines?
options: Because Saul was no longer seeking him
Because he feared he would perish by Saul's hand
Because he wanted to conquer more land
Because Achish invited him
questions.correctAnswer: Because he feared he would perish by Saul's hand
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 27:1, David said in his heart that he would perish one day by the hand of Saul, so he decided to escape to the land of the Philistines.

questions.question: With how many men did David pass over to Achish, king of Gath?
options: Four hundred
Five hundred
Six hundred
Seven hundred
questions.correctAnswer: Six hundred
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:2 states that David arose and passed over with the six hundred men that were with him unto Achish.

questions.question: Who was the king of Gath that David dwelt with?
options: Achish, son of Maoch
Saul, son of Kish
Abner, son of Ner
Nabal, son of Carmelite
questions.correctAnswer: Achish, son of Maoch
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 27:2, David went to Achish, the son of Maoch, king of Gath.

questions.question: Which two wives did David dwell with at Gath?
options: Michal and Bathsheba
Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the Carmelitess
Ruth and Esther
Sarah and Rebekah
questions.correctAnswer: Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the Carmelitess
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:3 states that David dwelt with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal's wife.

questions.question: What was the reaction of Saul when he heard that David fled to Gath?
options: He immediately sent soldiers to kill David
He sought David no more
He rejoiced and made peace
He sent gifts to David
questions.correctAnswer: He sought David no more
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:4 says that when it was told to Saul that David fled to Gath, he sought no more again for him.

questions.question: True or False: David believed escaping to the land of the Philistines would make Saul despair of seeking him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 27:1, David thought that by escaping to the Philistines, Saul would despair of him and not seek him any more.

questions.question: True or False: David took only some of his men and left the rest behind when he went to Achish.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:2 states that David passed over with the six hundred men that were with him, implying he took all his men.

questions.question: What did David request from Achish after he found grace in his eyes?
options: A place in some town in the country to dwell
To be made king of Gath
To be given gold and silver
To return to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: A place in some town in the country to dwell
questions.explanation: Though from a later verse, David's request is mentioned in 1 Samuel 27:5 where he asks Achish for a place in some town in the country to dwell.

questions.question: Which town did Achish give to David to dwell in?
options: Gath
Ziklag
Jerusalem
Hebron
questions.correctAnswer: Ziklag
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:6 states that Achish gave David Ziklag to dwell in.

questions.question: How long did David dwell in the country of the Philistines?
options: Six months
One year and four months
Two years
Three years
questions.correctAnswer: One year and four months
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 27:7, David dwelt in the country of the Philistines for a full year and four months.

questions.question: True or False: Saul continued to seek David after he fled to Gath.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:4 clearly states that after Saul heard David fled to Gath, he sought no more again for him.

questions.question: Which statement comes first in 1 Samuel 27:1?
options: David decides to flee to the Philistines
Saul seeks David throughout Israel
David marries Abigail
Achish gives David Ziklag
questions.correctAnswer: David decides to flee to the Philistines
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 27:1, the first event is David deciding in his heart to escape to the Philistines to avoid Saul.

questions.question: True or False: David dwelt in the royal city of Gath with Achish.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 27:5, David asks Achish for a place in some town in the country rather than dwelling in the royal city with him.

questions.question: David fled to the land of which people according to 1 Samuel 27?
options: Moabites
Amalekites
Philistines
Ammonites
questions.correctAnswer: Philistines
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:1 mentions that David escaped into the land of the Philistines.

questions.question: Who was Abigail before marrying David?
options: A Jezreelitess
Wife of Nabal, a Carmelite
Daughter of Achish
A Philistine princess
questions.correctAnswer: Wife of Nabal, a Carmelite
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:3 identifies Abigail as the Carmelitess, Nabal's wife, before she was David's wife.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 27 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 27 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Why did David ask Achish for a town in the country instead of dwelling in the royal city with him?
options: Because he wanted a place to hide from Saul
Because he did not want to live among the Philistines
Because he felt it was better not to dwell in the royal city with the king
Because he wanted to rule a town himself
questions.correctAnswer: Because he felt it was better not to dwell in the royal city with the king
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:5 shows David asking Achish for a town in the country so that he may dwell there, reasoning that he should not dwell in the royal city with Achish. This reflects David's humility and desire for safety without causing tension.

questions.question: What gift did Achish give to David as a place to live?
options: Gath
Ziklag
Jerusalem
Hebron
questions.correctAnswer: Ziklag
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 27:6, Achish gave David the town of Ziklag to dwell in. This town remained associated with the kings of Judah thereafter, highlighting its significance.

questions.question: How long did David live in the land of the Philistines?
options: Six months
One year and four months
Two years
Three years
questions.correctAnswer: One year and four months
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:7 states that David dwelt in the country of the Philistines for a full year and four months. This time period reflects his strategic move to escape Saul.

questions.question: Which nations did David and his men invade while living in the land of the Philistines?
options: The Amalekites, Geshurites, and Gezrites
The Israelites and Moabites
The Edomites and Philistines
The Egyptians and Canaanites
questions.correctAnswer: The Amalekites, Geshurites, and Gezrites
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:8 identifies the Geshurites, Gezrites, and Amalekites as the nations David and his men invaded. These were longstanding inhabitants of the land near Egypt.

questions.question: What does David’s strategy of asking for a town outside the royal city teach us about humility?
options: Humility involves seeking honor and high status
Humility is shown by avoiding conflict and living quietly
Humility means refusing to accept help from others
Humility requires confrontation to prove oneself
questions.correctAnswer: Humility is shown by avoiding conflict and living quietly
questions.explanation: David’s request in 1 Samuel 27:5 to live in a town rather than the royal city demonstrates humility and a desire to avoid unnecessary conflict, teaching us the biblical virtue of humility in difficult situations.

questions.question: How does David’s choice to dwell among the Philistines reflect trust in God's providence?
options: He relied on his own strength rather than God
He sought protection in an enemy’s land, trusting God would protect him
He abandoned faith in God by hiding
He tried to make peace through political alliances
questions.correctAnswer: He sought protection in an enemy’s land, trusting God would protect him
questions.explanation: David’s move to the Philistines as seen in 1 Samuel 27:1-7 shows a strategic trust in God’s protection despite the danger, demonstrating faith in God’s providence in uncertain times.

questions.question: What lesson about integrity can be drawn from David’s actions against the Geshurites, Gezrites, and Amalekites?
options: He spared many to keep alliances strong
He acted decisively and did not leave witnesses to report against him
He pretended to be loyal to the Philistines
He avoided all conflict to maintain peace
questions.correctAnswer: He acted decisively and did not leave witnesses to report against him
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:9-11 reveals David’s deliberate actions to leave no survivors who could report back, illustrating his careful and resolute approach to safeguard his position, which can be seen as a lesson in integrity regarding cautious obedience to his goals.

questions.question: Based on 1 Samuel 27:6-7, what does the granting of Ziklag and David’s stay there teach about God’s timing and provision?
options: God’s provision is immediate and always in visible ways
God provides places of refuge and timing that suit His purposes
God’s provision means constant comfort and ease
God’s provision is irrelevant to strategic decisions
questions.correctAnswer: God provides places of refuge and timing that suit His purposes
questions.explanation: David’s receiving Ziklag (verse 6) and dwelling there for over a year (verse 7) show that God’s provision can include strategic refuge and timing for growth and protection, teaching patience and reliance on God’s plan.

questions.question: True or False: David requested a place to live in the royal city with Achish to gain favor and influence.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:5 clearly states David asked for a town in the country, not to dwell in the royal city, indicating a desire for separation rather than seeking influence.

questions.question: What does David’s destruction of the Amalekites and other groups teach us about dealing with persistent threats?
options: We should forgive immediately without caution
We should act decisively to remove threats to our safety
We should avoid all conflict at any cost
We should rely only on human strength
questions.correctAnswer: We should act decisively to remove threats to our safety
questions.explanation: David’s actions in 1 Samuel 27:8-9 show a decisive approach to dealing with hostile groups, illustrating the biblical principle of prudence and protecting oneself from persistent danger.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 27:10-11 show David’s concern for loyalty and secrecy?
options: David openly shared his plans with Achish
David lied about his raids to Achish to protect his men
David left survivors to spread news of his loyalty
David saved captives to use as messengers
questions.correctAnswer: David lied about his raids to Achish to protect his men
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 show David telling Achish he raided areas south of Judah, while actually attacking other groups, emphasizing his careful management of information to maintain loyalty and secrecy.

questions.question: True or False: Achish believed that David was hated by Israel and therefore trusted him as his servant forever.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:12 states Achish believed David because he thought Israel abhorred him, which led Achish to trust David permanently as his servant.

questions.question: A fellow believer feels the need to relocate for safety amid persecution. Based on David’s example in 1 Samuel 27, what biblical truth applies?
options: Abandon faith to blend in with the new culture
Seek God’s guidance and trust His provision even when dwelling among strangers
Avoid all places that are not their homeland
Use deception to gain personal advantage
questions.correctAnswer: Seek God’s guidance and trust His provision even when dwelling among strangers
questions.explanation: David’s relocation to Philistine territory (1 Samuel 27:1-7) shows trusting God’s providence in unfamiliar and potentially hostile environments, teaching believers to seek God’s guidance and protection in trials.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 27:6 teach about the lasting impact of God’s provision?
options: God’s provision is temporary and soon forgotten
God’s provision can have enduring significance beyond immediate circumstances
God’s provision only benefits the recipient personally
God’s provision is unrelated to future generations
questions.correctAnswer: God’s provision can have enduring significance beyond immediate circumstances
questions.explanation: Verse 6 notes that Ziklag remained with the kings of Judah to this day, indicating God’s provision had lasting historical and spiritual impact beyond David’s time.

questions.question: True or False: David left survivors among the nations he attacked to report his actions to the Philistines.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:11 explicitly states David left neither man nor woman alive to report on his actions, ensuring no news would undermine his position among the Philistines.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 27 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 27.

questions.question: What did David do to the inhabitants of the land he attacked while living in the country of the Philistines?
options: He spared them all and took only livestock
He left neither man nor woman alive
He made peace treaties with them
He imprisoned the men and released the women
questions.correctAnswer: He left neither man nor woman alive
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:9 states that David smote the land and left neither man nor woman alive, taking away livestock and apparel.

questions.question: To which areas did David claim to have made his raids when asked by Achish?
options: Against the north of Israel
Against the south of Judah, Jerahmeelites, and Kenites
Against the land of the Philistines
Against the cities in Gath
questions.correctAnswer: Against the south of Judah, Jerahmeelites, and Kenites
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 27:10, David told Achish his raids were against the south of Judah, the Jerahmeelites, and the Kenites.

questions.question: Why did David kill all men and women in the lands he raided without sparing any to bring news to Gath?
options: To prevent them from warning others about his attacks
To enslave the survivors
To offer sacrifices to Achish
To gain favor with Saul
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent them from warning others about his attacks
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:11 explains David’s motive was to prevent any survivors from reporting to Gath, which would reveal his true activities.

questions.question: What belief did Achish hold about David after hearing his reports?
options: David was a traitor to Israel
David was hated by Israel and thus would serve Achish forever
David was planning to overthrow Achish
David was a loyal servant of Saul
questions.correctAnswer: David was hated by Israel and thus would serve Achish forever
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:12 shows Achish believed Israel hated David, so David would be his servant forever.

questions.question: Which town was given to David by Achish as a place to dwell?
options: Gath
Ziklag
Hebron
Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Ziklag
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:6 records that Achish gave David Ziklag, which remained under the kings of Judah.

questions.question: How long did David dwell in the country of the Philistines?
options: Six months
One year and four months
Two years
Three years
questions.correctAnswer: One year and four months
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:7 states that David stayed in the land of the Philistines for a full year and four months.

questions.question: Which peoples did David invade while living under Achish’s protection?
options: Amalekites, Geshurites, and Gezrites
Philistines, Moabites, and Edomites
Jebusites, Canaanites, and Hittites
Ammonites, Midianites, and Amalekites
questions.correctAnswer: Amalekites, Geshurites, and Gezrites
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:8 says David and his men invaded the Geshurites, Gezrites, and Amalekites.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in 1 Samuel 27:11 to emphasize David’s ruthless tactics?
options: Simile
Hyperbole
Repetition
Chiasm
questions.correctAnswer: Repetition
questions.explanation: Verse 11 repeats the phrase 'neither man nor woman alive' to emphasize the totality of David’s destruction, a form of repetition.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'smote' in 1 Samuel 27:9 most closely means what?
options: To bless or favor
To strike or kill
To hide or conceal
To build or establish
questions.correctAnswer: To strike or kill
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root "nakah" used here means 'to strike' or 'to kill,' indicating David’s violent attack (1 Samuel 27:9).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of seeking refuge among enemies as David did in 1 Samuel 27?
options: Genesis 39, where Joseph goes to Egypt
Exodus 1, where Israelites flee Egypt
1 Kings 19, where Elijah flees to the wilderness
Judges 6, where Gideon hides from Midianites
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 39, where Joseph goes to Egypt
questions.explanation: Like David fleeing to the Philistines, Joseph sought refuge in Egypt, illustrating a recurring biblical theme of flight to foreign lands for safety (Genesis 39).

questions.question: Which New Testament figure’s experience parallels David’s strategic alliance with an enemy king in 1 Samuel 27?
options: Paul’s mission in Roman territories
Jesus’s interaction with Herod
Peter’s visit to Cornelius
John the Baptist’s imprisonment
questions.correctAnswer: Paul’s mission in Roman territories
questions.explanation: Paul’s ministry involved navigating political powers and alliances in hostile Roman lands, similar to David’s alliance with Achish (Acts 21).

questions.question: What theme from Psalm 34 is foreshadowed by David’s time in Philistine territory described in 1 Samuel 27?
options: God delivers the righteous from all fears
The prosperity of the wicked
The judgment of enemies
The establishment of a kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: God delivers the righteous from all fears
questions.explanation: Psalm 34, traditionally attributed to David during distress, echoes the theme of God’s deliverance despite danger, as seen in David’s Philistine refuge (Psalm 34:19).

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 27 illustrate the theme of divine providence despite apparent compromise?
options: David’s success in raids shows God’s protection even in foreign lands
David’s exile results in his downfall
Saul’s forgiveness of David is evident
David becomes king immediately
questions.correctAnswer: David’s success in raids shows God’s protection even in foreign lands
questions.explanation: Though living among enemies, David’s military success and survival reflect God’s providential care (1 Samuel 27:9-12).

questions.question: True or False: Achish gave David a place to dwell in the royal city of Gath because he wanted to keep David close at hand.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:5 shows David asked for a town in the country rather than the royal city, and Achish granted Ziklag instead (1 Samuel 27:6).

questions.question: True or False: David’s ruthless raids and complete destruction of the inhabitants were intended to secure Achish’s trust by presenting himself as an enemy of Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 27:11-12 explains David’s tactic was to appear hostile to Israel so Achish would trust and keep him as a servant.

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 27 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 27 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological reason did David give in his heart for fleeing to the land of the Philistines?
options: To escape Saul's hand and cause Saul to despair of seeking him anymore
To conquer the Philistines and expand Israel's territory
To seek God's guidance among the Philistines
To unite with Saul against common enemies
questions.correctAnswer: To escape Saul's hand and cause Saul to despair of seeking him anymore
questions.explanation: David considered that he would perish one day by Saul's hand, so he chose to escape into the land of the Philistines, causing Saul to despair of seeking him any more (1 Samuel 27:1).

questions.question: What does David's request to Achish for a town to dwell in rather than the royal city reveal about his character or strategy?
options: A desire to avoid suspicion by not staying in the royal city
A disdain for royalty and city life
A wish to isolate himself for spiritual meditation
A plan to secretly rally Philistine forces
questions.correctAnswer: A desire to avoid suspicion by not staying in the royal city
questions.explanation: David asked Achish for a place in some town in the country to dwell in, so he would not dwell in the royal city with Achish, revealing a strategic move to avoid attention (1 Samuel 27:5).

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by Achish granting David the town of Ziklag, which remained with the kings of Judah to that day?
options: God's providential preservation of David's lineage and legacy
The sovereignty of Philistine kings over Israel
The futility of Saul's reign
The necessity of political alliances for survival
questions.correctAnswer: God's providential preservation of David's lineage and legacy
questions.explanation: Achish gave David Ziklag, a town that pertained to the kings of Judah, showing God's providential care in preserving David's future kingdom (1 Samuel 27:6).

questions.question: How long did David dwell in the country of the Philistines, and what might this duration suggest about God's timing in David's life?
options: One year and four months; indicating a divinely appointed period of testing and preparation
Six months; indicating a brief refuge before returning
Two years; showing prolonged exile
Three months; indicating a quick resolution
questions.correctAnswer: One year and four months; indicating a divinely appointed period of testing and preparation
questions.explanation: David dwelt in the country of the Philistines for a full year and four months, suggesting God allowed a specific season for trial and growth before his eventual kingship (1 Samuel 27:7).

questions.question: What does the violence of David's attacks on the Geshurites, Gezrites, and Amalekites reveal about the nature of conflict and survival in this period of Israel's history?
options: The harsh realities and total warfare characteristic of ancient Near Eastern tribal conflicts
David's rejection of God's commands for mercy
The Philistines' influence on David's moral decline
A deviation from God's covenant principles
questions.correctAnswer: The harsh realities and total warfare characteristic of ancient Near Eastern tribal conflicts
questions.explanation: David smote these nations, leaving neither man nor woman alive, reflecting the brutal nature of warfare in that era as a means of survival and dominance (1 Samuel 27:8-9).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Achish's belief that Israel abhorred David and that he would serve him forever?
options: God's permissive will allowing human deception
God's omniscience in revealing truth directly to Achish
God's wrath upon David
God's providence allowing David's refuge
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence allowing David's refuge
questions.explanation: Achish believed David had been rejected by Israel and would serve him forever, showing God's providential hand in using even misunderstanding to protect David (1 Samuel 27:12).

questions.question: What theological insight arises from combining David's flight to Philistia (verses 1-2) and his destructive raids on neighboring peoples (verses 8-9)?
options: David's human sinfulness coexists with God's sovereign protection over him
David's complete obedience to God's commands
The justification of violence by covenant promises
The Philistines' role as God's chosen people
questions.correctAnswer: David's human sinfulness coexists with God's sovereign protection over him
questions.explanation: David flees Saul out of fear yet engages in total warfare, showing his flawed humanity, while God sovereignly preserves him for future kingship (1 Samuel 27:1-2, 8-9).

questions.question: How does the passage about David sparing no survivors to prevent news reaching Gath (verse 11) contribute to understanding the tension between David's political survival and moral conduct?
options: It reveals David's pragmatic but morally ambiguous actions to secure his safety
It portrays David as a perfect moral exemplar
It shows David's rejection of God's commands
It indicates David's alliance with Saul
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals David's pragmatic but morally ambiguous actions to secure his safety
questions.explanation: David spared no one to prevent news reaching Gath, illustrating a complex tension between political necessity and ethical compromise (1 Samuel 27:11).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do verses 4 and 12 convey about human rejection and divine purpose?
options: Human rejection (Saul's ceasing to seek David) can serve God's sovereign plan to establish David as servant under foreign rulers
Human rejection is always a sign of divine abandonment
Divine purpose depends on human approval
Saul's rejection nullifies David's legitimacy
questions.correctAnswer: Human rejection (Saul's ceasing to seek David) can serve God's sovereign plan to establish David as servant under foreign rulers
questions.explanation: Saul stopped seeking David (verse 4), and Achish believed David was rejected by Israel and would serve him forever (verse 12), showing God uses human rejection for His sovereign purposes (1 Samuel 27:4, 12).

questions.question: From an apologetics perspective, how does 1 Samuel 27:1-12 respond to the sceptic's claim that David's alliance with the Philistines shows him as a traitor to Israel?
options: The passage shows David's flight as a strategic refuge and God's providence in protecting him, not treason
It proves David was a political opportunist with no loyalty
It confirms David abandoned God's covenant for personal gain
It shows David was coerced by the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: The passage shows David's flight as a strategic refuge and God's providence in protecting him, not treason
questions.explanation: Though David lived among Philistines, he intended to escape Saul and God providentially preserved him, countering claims of treason (1 Samuel 27:1-12).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is implicitly revealed by David's survival despite Saul's persistent pursuit and David's morally complex actions in this chapter?
options: God's faithfulness to His covenant promises to David
God's immediate judgment on sinners
God's concealment of His will
God's partiality toward Saul
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness to His covenant promises to David
questions.explanation: Despite Saul's pursuit and David's actions, God faithfully preserves David per His covenant promises (1 Samuel 27:1-12).

questions.question: How does David's request for a town outside the royal city (verse 5) align with the biblical theme of humility and reliance on God rather than earthly power?
options: It reflects David's humble dependence on God rather than seeking status among Philistine royalty
It shows David's rejection of God's promises
It reveals David's ambition for the Philistine throne
It demonstrates David's fear of his own men
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects David's humble dependence on God rather than seeking status among Philistine royalty
questions.explanation: David preferred to dwell in a town, avoiding the royal city, signifying humility and trust in God's timing rather than political advantage (1 Samuel 27:5).

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does David’s residence in Philistine territory (verses 2-3) and his eventual kingship illustrate in the grand story of redemption?
options: God’s use of exile and foreign refuge to prepare the Messiah’s ancestor for kingship
The permanent defeat of Israel by its enemies
The failure of God's people to remain faithful
The rejection of God's covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: God’s use of exile and foreign refuge to prepare the Messiah’s ancestor for kingship
questions.explanation: David's stay in Philistine land foreshadows the Messiah's exile and preparation before kingship, fitting the redemptive narrative (1 Samuel 27:2-3).

questions.question: What synthesis doctrine arises from David's destruction of the Amalekites and his service to Achish (verses 9 and 12) regarding God's judgment and human agency?
options: God executes judgment through human agents who act within complex moral situations
God condones all human violence
Human actions are irrelevant to divine plans
David acted independently of God's will
questions.correctAnswer: God executes judgment through human agents who act within complex moral situations
questions.explanation: David’s destruction of old enemies and his service to Achish show God using David as an agent of judgment amid morally complex circumstances (1 Samuel 27:9, 12).

questions.question: How does David's statement that Saul will seek him no more (verse 1) connect to the biblical theme of God’s protection over His anointed servant?
options: It reflects God’s providential control over Saul’s pursuit to safeguard David
It shows David’s abandonment of faith in God
It predicts Saul’s ultimate victory
It indicates David’s self-reliance
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects God’s providential control over Saul’s pursuit to safeguard David
questions.explanation: David anticipates escape so Saul will cease pursuit, indicating God’s providential protection over His chosen servant (1 Samuel 27:1).
